subject: On-ramp plan: shifting Suncrest from on-demand to dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@suncrestbio.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.inference <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@suncrestbio.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transitioning from on-demand to dedicated: sizing & timeline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier. We ran the traffic report last quarter and we think moving from on-demand to a dedicated reservation is the next logical step to stabilize latency and control unit economics. A few data points from our side to help size the offer:
- Current steady-state: ~180M tokens / month (mixed chat + reranking).
- 95th percentile latency target: <400ms for chat flows (p95 per-token).
- Burst profile: occasional peaks ~3x baseline for 2–3 hours, ~6x for 20–30 minutes.
- Tolerance for preemption: low — up to 5% best-effort background work can be preemptible, but real-time chat must remain non-preempted.
- Preferred ramp: pilot for 4–6 weeks, then scale to production over 2–3 months.

Can you sketch a few reserved-capacity options (min-guaranteed GPUs, warm pool for bursts, activation windows, and suggested ramp schedule) plus indicative pricing and any startup credits for the pilot? Also call out what SLA/activation lead times we should expect and whether we can request an on-prem fallback for regulated jobs.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Engineering
Suncrest Bio

---

From: jonas_weber@redwood.inference <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>

Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transitioning from on-demand to dedicated: sizing & timeline

Elena —

Appreciate the detail — this is exactly what we need to put together a practical on-ramp. High-level options below; I attached a compact PDF and a pricing sheet for the math (Suncrest_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf, Suncrest_pricing-sheet_v2.xlsx).

Option A — Pilot (recommended first step)
- Dedicated pilot pool: 8 x A100 (or equivalent q4 quantized instances)
- Min guarantee: 4 GPUs reserved during pilot window; burst borrow up to 8 if capacity allows
- Duration: 4–6 weeks
- Use: validate prefix/KV cache performance, routing policies, and QoS for real-time flows
- Activation lead time: 7–10 business days from PO
- Pricing: pilot discount (35% off list) + 2 weeks free warm credits for burst testing

Option B — Production on-ramp (recommended default)
- Initial min floor: 16 GPUs reserved (non-preemptible for chat)
- Warm pool: additional 8 GPUs billed on standby (hot-warm) for <1s warmup to reduce tail latency
- Burst credits: 10% monthly burst allowance (temporary scale up to +2x for short windows)
- Ramp: move to 48 GPUs within 90 days based on traffic triggers (we define triggers together)
- Activation lead time: 10–14 business days for full slate; staged provisioning can begin within 72 hours for the warm pool
- Pricing: 20% commit discount; additional volume tiers at 32/48 GPUs

Option C — Anchored production (long-term capacity commitment)
- Min floor: 32 GPUs (non-preemptible)
- Burst & reserve: 32 warm-burst GPUs (bursting to 64) with preemption allowed only on non-latency-critical workloads
- Ramp schedule: structured over 6 months with monthly activation milestones and burn-credit offsets for early activation
- SLA: 99.95% uptime, latency SLOs tied to per-route p95 targets; premium SLA add-on for stricter latency guarantees
- Pricing: enterprise tier (negotiable), preferred queueing and region placement for production traffic

Operational notes / differentiators
- We’ll set up automatic KV/prefix caching and progressive batching with per-route latency controls to reduce per-token cost without harming p95.
- Smart routing: traffic can be routed to on-demand or a backfill pool if you need to preserve availability during scaling events.
- On‑prem fallback: we support a hybrid private deployment for regulated jobs. That requires an additional appliance package and a 30–45 day provisioning schedule, scoped separately.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Run the 4–6 week Pilot (Option A) to validate latencies and routing.
2) If pilot passes the p95 target and throughput checks, commit to Option B with a 90-day ramp.
3) Add an on-prem fallback annex to the contract if you need in-region air-gapped compute.

I’ve copied Marissa (solutions lead) and Karthik (deal lead) so we can align discounts and the activation runbook. PDF/pricing attached. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the options.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Transitioning from on-demand to dedicated: sizing & timeline

Marissa / Karthik —

Looping you both in. Quick read: Suncrest wants a pilot then a 2–3 month on-ramp to stabilize p95 & cost. They’re sensitive to preemption on chat flows (max ~5%). Recommend we push Option B as default for commercial terms: 16 min floor, 8 warm pool, ramp to 48 in 90 days. Call out two concession levers: activation lead time (shave to 72 hours for warm pool) and a 10% onboarding credit if they sign within 10 business days.

Questions:
- Marissa: ok to offer the additional onboarding credit (10% pilot credit) and 72-hour warm pool SLA as a one-time concession?
- Karthik: how is Suncrest’s seat in our pipeline for Q3 quota — do we want to offer a performance or volume-based rebate instead of deeper up-front discount?

I’ll prepare a short one-pager for the procurement team with DocuSign-ready language once we confirm concessions.

Thanks,
Jonas

Thanks for the clear options and the fast turnaround on the PDF/pricing. Procurement has reviewed Option B and prefers the 16 -> 48 ramp but asked for two items before routing to legal: a) a 7-calendar-day activation SLA for the warm pool (they want the ability to turn it on within a week), and b) a single DocuSign with the pilot terms + the ramp schedule annexed. They also asked whether we can commit to a 30-day pilot cancellation window with no early-termination fees.

If we can confirm the 7-day activation for the warm pool and the cancellation window, Procurement will sign and we can get PO issued by next Friday. They also asked for a one-page operations runbook outlining throttling/route overrides so their SREs can validate the p95 targets.

Can you confirm (yes/no) on the two asks and send a DocuSign link for the pilot + ramp annex?
